title: Sell Mineral Rights in Goldsmith, TX
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Goldsmith, TX | Royalty Buyer
metaDescription: Goldsmith, TX sits over one of the oldest producing fields in Ector County. See how legacy and new production both factor into your mineral value.
heroLead: Goldsmith has a name that sounds almost too perfect for an oil town, and the field underneath it has been producing since long before horizontal drilling existed.
intro: The Goldsmith field is one of the older producing areas in Ector County, with vertical wells that have been running for decades now sitting alongside newer horizontal Wolfcamp development on nearby acreage. If your family's minerals are tied to this area, there's a real chance your royalty check reflects some of that long production history.

sections.heading: An old field with new activity nearby
paragraphs: Legacy vertical production around Goldsmith continues at modest but steady rates in many units, while newer horizontal wells on adjacent acreage have added another layer of production in recent years. I look at each contributing well rather than assuming a single decline pattern.

sections.heading: What I need to give you a real number
paragraphs: A division order or recent check stub is the fastest path to an honest range. Old or modest-looking legacy production is still worth evaluating properly rather than dismissing.

sections.heading: Inherited fractions in an old field
paragraphs: Because Goldsmith field production dates back so far, it's common for ownership to be split among many heirs across multiple generations, some of whom may not even realize what they own. I buy individual fractional shares directly, no matter how small.

sections.heading: How the process runs
paragraphs: Once I have your paperwork, I build a range within a couple of days and explain the well history behind it. There's no cost or obligation to finding out what your interest is worth.

sections.heading: Why the old field still matters
paragraphs: A field that's been producing this long tends to have well-documented history, which actually makes valuation more precise, not less. I'd rather work from decades of real data than guess at a newer, thinly documented unit.

faqs.question: Is my Goldsmith-area interest from an old well still worth anything?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. Legacy production in this field still generates real royalty income, and I value it against actual data rather than writing it off because the well is old.

faqs.question: Is there new drilling happening near Goldsmith too?
faqs.answer: Yes, horizontal Wolfcamp development has continued on acreage near the older field, which can add value to nearby undeveloped or lightly developed interests.

faqs.question: How do I know what my decimal interest actually is?
faqs.answer: Your division order will show it directly. If you don't have one, send me what you have and I'll help track it down through the operator or state records.
